midsectionContent.content: I host weekly office hours every Sunday from 2pm-5pm at the Washington County Democratic Headquarters. I invite you to come by to share your concerns and discuss your ideas for our community.
midsectionContent.topRight: # My Agenda for Justice of the Peace

As your Justice of the Peace, my primary goal is to serve the people of Washington County with integrity, transparency, and a commitment to fair and timely justice. I believe that every resident deserves to be heard and every concern deserves a thoughtful response.

I will make it my priority to be accessible to everyone in our community. By maintaining regular office hours and actively seeking out feedback from residents, I will ensure that your concerns are understood and addressed promptly.

Justice should be timely. I am committed to handling civil disputes with a focus on fair, common-sense resolutions that help our neighbors move forward. I will work to ensure that the process is straightforward and easy to navigate for all parties involved.

The legal system can be confusing. I will strive to provide clear, honest, and easy-to-understand information about the roles and services of the Justice of the Peace office, ensuring that residents feel empowered and informed.
I will uphold the highest standards of ethics and accountability. My focus will always be on serving the community's interests and upholding the law with honesty and respect.
*Let’s work together to keep Washington County a fair and thriving place to live.*

about.title: About Me
content: I am a wife and mom of three who works in health care as a registrar. My family and I moved to Arkansas in 2021 from the Pacific Northwest as an adventure and for a change of pace from living and working in the Portland metro area. I instantly fell in love with NWA. My boys have thrived in Springdale Public Schools, and my oldest is a student at the University of Arkansas. I’m grateful for the opportunities this move has afforded us and I want to serve my community in a meaningful way.

I believe that the most important thing a representative can do is to listen to their constituents and bring their concerns to the table they’ve been elected to sit at. I have never run for public office, and I won’t be at all offended if people don’t vote for me. What I can promise is this: If you trust me enough to vote for me for Justice of the Peace, I will make it my number one priority to hear what you have to say and act on it. I will work diligently for you.
